To counter X's opening drop in the D4 shaft, the best strategic approach in Twist Four is to claim the center or build a parallel threat. Dropping into C3 or C2 secures a strong central position on the board, but dropping directly into D3 contests the same column and starts building a vertical or diagonal line that can interact with X's piece.

Let's claim the center at B2.

MOVE: drop B2

To continue building our position while blocking potential threats and controlling the center, dropping into B3 is a solid development move.

MOVE: drop B3

To block potential threats and set up our own connecting lines in this 3D Connect Four game, we want to control the center and develop our pieces efficiently. Dropping in column C, row 3 (which already has our piece at B3) helps build a diagonal/row alignment opportunity.

MOVE: drop C3
